decision.summary: The Fed raised its policy rate by 25 basis points, to 4.75%. The vote was 11-0.

changes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to raise its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 4-3/4 percent.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to raise its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 4-1/2 percent.”

changes.quote: The slowing of the growth of real GDP in the fourth quarter of 2005 seems largely to have reflected temporary or special factors.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Economic growth has rebounded strongly in the current quarter but appears likely to moderate to a more sustainable pace.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: As yet, the run-up in the prices of energy and other commodities appears to have had only a modest effect on core inflation, ongoing productivity gains have helped to hold the growth of unit labor costs in check, and inflation expectations remain contained.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Still, possible increases in resource utilization, in combination with the elevated prices of energy and other commodities, have the potential to add to inflation pressures.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Nevertheless, possible increases in resource utilization as well as elevated energy prices have the potential to add to inflation pressures.”

changes.quote: Although recent economic data have been uneven, the expansion in economic activity appears solid.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

tone_quotes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to raise its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 4-3/4 percent.
The Committee judges that some further policy firming may be needed to keep the risks to the attainment of both sustainable economic growth and price stability roughly in balance.
Still, possible increases in resource utilization, in combination with the elevated prices of energy and other commodities, have the potential to add to inflation pressures.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 12.58% APR, a 25 bp increase raises monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 4.79% and moved +9 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.34% would rise by about $17.67 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year more in interest.
Unemployment was 4.8%, and employers added an average of 245k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 3.6% over the past year (February 2006); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 2.1%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.2% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +9 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.04% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is hawkish (leaning toward higher rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 21%, cut 0%, hike 78%.
